answer: Seniority-weighted action quotas resist sybils: the number of consequential actions an identity may take per epoch scales with its SENIORITY (epochs survived), so fresh fakes are capped at a trickle while aged honest identities act freely. A mesa of day-one fakes each gets the minimal newcomer quota; the prism of full action capacity only opens with accumulated tenure. An attacker's fleet wanders at the newcomer floor for a long time — aggregate throughput bounded by how many fakes have genuinely aged — so instant mass creation yields instant mass THROTTLING, not power.
